name: PrimPersonObject::ChooseAction (FindBestAction: rank the scored actions and take one)
notes: Lane AF. Hooked (not yet run in-game). Differential test: 12,000 seeds over real heap vectors of ActionRecord / ScoreRecord in the person, fake environment, services, person, sink and held interactions, the random generator as a real cRZRandom in the world, 0x515c80 stood in for by a recording function, exception injection (the vectors are described and destroyed in the unwind too); coverage requires a choice, no choice, a rank above the first, the log closed and an empty list. 15 mutants killed; one survivor is equivalent (the early return when the walk reaches the wanted rank without score recording: every later record has a higher rank and is skipped anyway). The original returns leftover register contents; callers ignore it (not compared). The interaction checks it makes (CheckInteraction, 0x515c80) are real on both sides in the test (the check world, tests/simantics_autonomy_checkworld.h).

name: PrimPersonObject::StartChosenAction (FindBestAction: make the chosen action the next one)
notes: Lane AF. Hooked (not yet run in-game). Differential test: 12,000 seeds with exception injection over real heap vectors (chosen records, the recent-action memory with the game's allocator, grown from full), the object table and the owner / tracker / host chain as fakes; coverage: started, refused by the minimum-score mode (incl. a NaN score), no choice. 15 mutants killed. ORIGINAL-BUG (not generated by the test, the original crashes): a chosen action whose stack object is gone or whose owner is missing, and a tracker interface that cannot be obtained, are dereferenced without a check. The recent-action vector uses the game's allocator (RZMemory), as the original's does, so original code can free its blocks.

name: PrimPersonObject::ScoreInteraction (FindBestAction: score one interaction into an ActionRecord)
notes: Lane AF. Hooked (not yet run in-game). Differential test: 30,000 seeds with exception injection over the score world (tests/simantics_autonomy_scoreworld.h): the score factor 0x512860, the BCON lookups, the option mask, the tree flag map and the game allocator are real on both sides, fakes (floats too) behind the vtables, the recent-action memory built from the world's own object ids, thresholds including zero and tiny; every field of the records it builds is compared, with the vectors grown from full too. The 5 argument bytes: gathered / checked are read as bytes (the callers push dwords). 34 mutants over this file and ScorePending: all killed except `threshold >= score`, which is equivalent in practice (it needs a score exactly equal to 0.2 or 0.05; with a threshold of zero or 1e-6 the 1e-5 minimum rejects the same scores). Arities: the callers' extra pushes (Prim03 pushes three arguments to GetPersonData and one to the kind list) belong to the next call; ours pass each slot's own count.
